name: Croton
lesson_scope: Morphology-first comparison of six canonical learner species. Genus lesson enrichment only: preserve all existing species, image attributions, source decisions, range HOLDs, and taxonomy concepts. No new species added.

project_scope.species_count_note: All six already occur in data/manifest.json; installed does not imply certified target-zone native.

shared_genus_pattern.look_here_first: Inspect the lower leaf surface with magnification for stellate (star-shaped) or scalelike hairs, then find a pistillate flower or capsule. On a flowering plant, check if male and female flowers share the same plant, the number/division of styles, pistillate sepal posture and whether capsules are smooth or warty.
shared_genus_pattern.vegetative: Herbs through shrubs, usually alternate simple leaves; leaf outlines vary widely. Stellate or lepidote hairs are an important Croton clue. Gray-looking leaves alone do not make a species ID.
shared_genus_pattern.reproductive: Flowers generally small and unisexual, often with lower pistillate and upper staminate flowers along mixed inflorescences in monoecious species. Dioecious species have male and female flowers on separate plants.
shared_genus_pattern.fruit: Usually a three-part capsule in the current group; prairie tea is exceptional: two locules with only one fertile, yielding an apparently one-seeded, follicle-like fruit.
shared_genus_pattern.family_tie_breaker: Against Euphorbia, look for Croton's stellate/scalelike hairs and ordinary separate tiny unisexual flowers rather than cyathia. Against Acalypha, inspect reproductive spikes and the characteristic Acalypha pistillate bracts rather than relying on leaf outline.

central_texas_look_here_first: 1. Woody subshrub with finely serrulate leaves? Check Croton fruticulosus.
2. Annual with separate male and female plants and warty capsules? Check Croton texensis.
3. Annual with BROWN-DOTTED lower leaf surfaces, TWO bifid styles (four tips) and one-seeded fruit? Croton monanthogynus (prairie tea).
4. Low, basal-branching annual without brown-dotted lower leaf surfaces, THREE bifid styles (six tips) and smooth three-seeded capsule? Croton lindheimerianus.

5. Robust woolly annual with longer many-parted styles and conspicuous persistent pistillate sepals? Compare Croton lindheimeri versus TRUE Croton capitatus on sepal posture and leaf tips. Do not rely on old variety labels.

comparison_matrix.monanthogynus: Small annual; often many branches near base.
comparison_matrix.lindheimerianus: Small annual; often dichotomous branching near base.
comparison_matrix.texensis: Annual; loosely branching toward upper stem.
comparison_matrix.lindheimeri: Larger annual, commonly with stronger upright main axis.
comparison_matrix.capitatus: Woolly annual, variable; habit alone insufficient.

comparison_matrix.texensis: Dioecious; separate male and female plants.

comparison_matrix.lindheimerianus: Entire; variable lanceolate to almost round.
comparison_matrix.capitatus: Entire; some leaves obtuse or mucronate.

comparison_matrix.monanthogynus: Some stellate hairs DARK-CENTERED, creating brown-dot effect abaxially.
comparison_matrix.lindheimerianus: Stellate hairs without brown dot effect.
comparison_matrix.fruticulosus: Stellate hairs; inspect woody stems and serrulation.
comparison_matrix.lindheimeri: Ochraceous yellow-brown woolly hairs on young growth; no brown-dot effect.
comparison_matrix.capitatus: Pale whitish to yellowish stellate wool; no brown-dot effect.

comparison_matrix.monanthogynus: Two styles, each bifid: FOUR terminal segments.
comparison_matrix.lindheimerianus: Three styles, each bifid: SIX terminal segments.
comparison_matrix.texensis: Three strongly multifid styles: 12–32+ terminal segments.
comparison_matrix.fruticulosus: Three bifid styles: SIX terminal segments.
comparison_matrix.lindheimeri: Three repeatedly forked styles: typically TWELVE terminal segments.
comparison_matrix.capitatus: Three repeatedly forked styles: typically 12–18 or more terminal segments.

comparison_matrix.monanthogynus: Five relatively short sepals; essentially one-seeded smooth capsule.
comparison_matrix.lindheimerianus: Five to six short sepals, about 3 mm; smooth three-locular capsule.
comparison_matrix.fruticulosus: Five short sepals, about 2.2 mm; smooth capsule.
comparison_matrix.lindheimeri: Seven to eight woolly sepals about 5–7 mm; tips straight or slightly incurved, not recurved.
comparison_matrix.capitatus: Six to nine long persistent sepals, often 7–10 mm or longer in fruit, tips flaring or recurved outward.

comparison_matrix.monanthogynus: PASS; brown-dot hairs + four style tips strongest.
comparison_matrix.lindheimerianus: PASS; distinguish from C. monanthogynus by underside and style count.
comparison_matrix.texensis: PASS; sex system and warty fruit first.
comparison_matrix.fruticulosus: PASS; woody base and leaf serrulation first.
comparison_matrix.lindheimeri: RANGE UNRESOLVED; not counted native; old C. capitatus var. lindheimeri resolves here.
comparison_matrix.capitatus: TAXON-CONCEPT UNRESOLVED locally; older C. capitatus var. lindheimeri records DO NOT certify true C. capitatus.

head_to_head.split: Prairie tea: dark-centered stars look brown-dotted, two bifid styles/four tips, effectively one seed. Lindheimer's croton: no brown dots, three bifid styles/six tips, three-locular capsule.
head_to_head.sterile_caution: If a leaf underside is too small to resolve with a field lens and no female flowers/fruit are present, leave the species tentative.

head_to_head.look_here_first: Brown-dot hairs versus dioecious flowers / warty fruit.
head_to_head.split: Prairie tea monoecious with one-seeded smooth fruit; Texas croton dioecious with narrow leaves and wart-covered three-part capsules.
head_to_head.sterile_caution: A lone male Texas croton plant cannot establish dioecy by itself; seek a female plant or fruit before asserting the distinction.

head_to_head.look_here_first: Female sepals on mature inflorescences, backed by leaf tips and young-stem color.
head_to_head.split: C. lindheimeri has more ochraceous young wool, mostly acute leaf apices, and straight to slightly incurved sepals; true C. capitatus more often has some blunt/mucronate leaves and long sepals recurving outward after anthesis.
head_to_head.sterile_caution: Historical 'C. capitatus var. lindheimeri' belongs with C. lindheimeri; do not show a mislabeled historical voucher as proof of true C. capitatus. Both scientific statuses stay unresolved for target-zone metrics.

head_to_head.look_here_first: Stem base and teeth along leaf margin, then sex system/fruit.
head_to_head.split: C. fruticulosus has woody stems, finely serrulate foliage, and bisexual racemes on one plant. C. texensis is an herbaceous dioecious annual with largely entire narrow leaves and warty fruit.
head_to_head.sterile_caution: Photograph the basal woody portion; a shoot-tip closeup does not prove shrub versus annual.

head_to_head.look_here_first: Female sepal length and style branching.
head_to_head.split: C. lindheimerianus has short pistillate sepals (~3 mm) and styles with six ultimate tips; C. lindheimeri has longer woolly sepals (~5–7 mm) and repeatedly forked styles, often twelve ultimate tips.
head_to_head.sterile_caution: Leaf fuzz alone can overlap; use a magnified female flower.

visual_comparison.title: Croton — find the leaf hairs, styles and fruit
visual_comparison.subtitle: Whole-plant faces are starting references only. The hard species splits need actual underside, female flower, and capsule macros.
visual_comparison.memory_rule: WOODY + tiny leaf teeth → fruticulosus. Separate male/female plants + WARTY fruit → texensis. Brown-dot hairs + FOUR style tips + one seed → monanthogynus. No brown dots + SIX style tips → lindheimerianus. Woolly robust pair → female sepal orientation and leaf tips: lindheimeri vs true capitatus.

study_cautions: Most Croton leaves are alternate, yet leaves crowd near some inflorescences; do not call the apparent leaf clusters a reliable opposite-leaf arrangement.
Look at pistillate (female) flowers to count the style branches; a male-only stem cannot show them.
The terms 'goatweed', 'doveweed' and 'croton' are reused across species and are not diagnostic.
Brown-dotted underside refers to dark centers in star-shaped hairs, not disease or reddish glands.
Croton capitatus and Croton lindheimeri historical synonymy is a real trap; never silently merge or count them both from the same old voucher.
Installed learner taxa do not all meet the three-county native certification criterion; do not convert two unresolved records into target-native PASS.
Existing images are provisional faces; do not label these as diagnostic micrographs when the key trait is not visibly resolved.

targeted_handoff.ordering: Start monanthogynus vs lindheimerianus (abaxial stellate hair dark centers and 4-vs-6 style tips); then C. texensis warty fruit; then C. fruticulosus woody base/serrulate margin; then C. lindheimeri vs verified true C. capitatus mature sepals.
targeted_handoff.photo_policy: Existing project/user/Joey exact-species photos first; then exact verified rights-appropriate outside sources, preserving photographer, license and observation URL. No substituting look-alike species. Check arrows land on actual structures.
targeted_handoff.preserve: Species native-range states, provisional images, and underlying taxonomic holds; photo polish is nonblocking for learner use.

genus_diagnostics.hair_character: Stellate (star-shaped) or scale-like hairs on at least some foliage or stems; check a true hair structure with a hand lens.
genus_diagnostics.leaves: Simple mostly alternate leaves; margins and habit vary across species.
genus_diagnostics.flowers: Small unisexual flowers; pistillate and staminate parts on one monoecious plant or on separate dioecious plants, depending on species.
genus_diagnostics.female_parts: Female styles and their branching are a particularly strong species-level character: 4 versus 6 versus many terminal arms.
genus_diagnostics.fruits: Usually a three-part capsule; C. monanthogynus is an exceptional one-fertile-locule species that appears one-seeded.

shared_traits: Look for star-shaped/scalelike hairs; generic gray fuzz or a brown stem is not sufficient.
Check small unisexual flowers, often on a common mixed inflorescence, then inspect the female style branches.
Leaves are usually alternate and simple, but leaf shape, tooth pattern and woody versus annual growth vary by species.
Most have a multi-part capsule; prairie tea has a distinctive effectively one-seeded capsule.
priority: 1. Woody perennial/subshrub base and finely serrulate leaf edges → C. fruticulosus.
2. Female versus male plants and distinct warty capsule → C. texensis.
3. Dark-brown-centered stellate hairs on lower leaf surface; four style tips → C. monanthogynus.
4. Lower surface without dark dots; six style tips → C. lindheimerianus.
5. Woolly robust pair: female sepal curvature, young-hair color, and mature leaf tips → C. lindheimeri vs true C. capitatus.
6. Do not count C. lindheimeri or C. capitatus as target-zone-certified natives until scientific holds are resolved.
study_strategy.warning: CAUTION: C. capitatus and C. lindheimeri have historic synonym/variety confusion. Their learner admission does not certify local nativity; do not reuse a C. capitatus var. lindheimeri specimen as evidence of true C. capitatus.
